In 7-dimensional [[geometry]], there are 71 [[uniform 7-polytope|uniform polytopes]] with A<sub>7</sub> symmetry. There is one self-dual regular form, the [[7-simplex]] with 8 vertices.

Each can be visualized as symmetric [[orthographic projection]]s in [[Coxeter plane]]s of the A<sub>7</sub> Coxeter group, and other subgroups.

__TOC__

== Graphs ==
Symmetric [[orthographic projection]]s of these 71 polytopes can be made in the A<sub>7</sub>, A<sub>6</sub>, A<sub>5</sub>, A<sub>4</sub>, A<sub>3</sub>, A<sub>2</sub> [[Coxeter plane]]s. A<sub>k</sub> has ''[k+1]'' symmetry. For even ''k'' and symmetrically ringed-diagrams, symmetry doubles to ''[2(k+1)]''.

These 71 polytopes are each shown in these 6 symmetry planes, with vertices and edges drawn, and vertices colored by the number of overlapping vertices in each projective position in progressive order: red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, purple, magenta, red-violet.
